summary.title: What is Linux From Scratch?
summary.one_liner: Linux From Scratch (LFS) gives step-by-step instructions for building your own customized Linux system entirely from source, and explains why you might want to.
keywords: how to build a linux system manually
alternative to downloading a linux distribution
takeaways: LFS is a project offering step-by-step instructions to build a customized Linux system entirely from source.
Building LFS teaches how Linux components work together and depend on each other.
A custom LFS build can be very compact; the page cites under 500 MB, and a minimal Apache-only system a little below 200 MB.
Compiling from source lets you audit the code and apply security patches yourself rather than waiting for binary packages.
A by-the-book LFS system is minimal; the BLFS project covers commonly used packages to add on top.
summary.summary: This introductory page from the Linux From Scratch project explains what LFS is: a set of step-by-step instructions for building a custom Linux system entirely from source. It argues the case for doing so, citing educational value in understanding Linux internals, a compact footprint (under 500 MB, or under 200 MB for a minimal Apache web server build), flexibility to tailor the system, and added security through source auditing and self-applied patches. It also notes that a by-the-book LFS system is minimal and that the BLFS project supplies commonly used add-on packages, and it lists the project's contributors.
